nodes.summary: For a sequence $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the initial-segment mean is the real number $m(a, n) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{j=1}^{n} a(j)$, with the convention $1 / 0 = 0$, so that $m(a, 0) = 0$.
nodes.title: Initial-segment mean

nodes.summary: For a sequence $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the unbiased initial-segment sample variance is the real number $v(a, n) = \frac{1}{n - 1} \sum_{j=1}^{n} \left(a(j) - \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=1}^{n} a(k)\right)^2$, with the convention $1 / 0 = 0$; in particular $v(a, 0) = v(a, 1) = 0$.
nodes.title: Initial-segment sample variance

nodes.summary: A sequence $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, indexed from $1$ (its value at $0$ is ignored), is admissible when $a(n) > 0$ for every $n \ge 1$ and there is $n_0 \ge 1$ such that $a(n) < a(n + 1)$ for every $n \ge n_0$.
nodes.title: Admissible sequences for Taylor's law

nodes.summary: A sequence $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, indexed from $1$ (its value at $0$ is ignored), satisfies Taylor's law asymptotically when it is admissible for Taylor's law and, writing $m(a, n)$ and $v(a, n)$ for its initial-segment mean and initial-segment sample variance, there are real numbers $c > 0$ and $b$ such that $v(a, n) / m(a, n)^b \to c$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Taylor's law, asymptotic form

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
